cues: Roots are where De Moivre really shines.
A complex number has infinitely many arguments, theta plus any multiple of two pi, and they all describe the same point.
Take the n th root: divide each argument by n.
The roots all have modulus r to the one over n, and are spaced two pi over n apart.
Exactly n of them, k from zero to n minus one.
text: Roots are where De Moivre really shines. A complex number has infinitely many arguments, theta plus any multiple of two pi, and they all describe the same point. Take the n th root: divide each argument by n. Now they are different! The roots all have modulus r to the one over n, and are spaced two pi over n apart. Exactly n of them, k from zero to n minus one.
